key_points.point_text: The author has been house hunting for almost a year in a strange market where some houses sit for a very long time while others sell within 1-2 days.
key_points.evidence_quote: He had been looking for a house for almost a year, longer than expected, in a weird market. / Houses either stay on the market a long time or are gone in usually 1-2 days.
key_points.reasoning: L005 captures the nearly one-year search in a weird market, L006 captures the bimodal market behavior with the 1-2 day timing intact.

key_points.point_text: On Wednesday afternoon the author offered the highest price he could afford on a house he liked, still about $30K below the asking price, hoping he might have a chance.
key_points.evidence_quote: Wednesday afternoon he put the highest price he could afford on a house he liked, about 30K below asking. / He hoped he might have a chance since the house was worth more than his offer.
key_points.reasoning: Timing (Wednesday afternoon), the maximum-affordable framing, the ~30K below-asking gap, and the hope are all preserved.

key_points.point_text: By Thursday 6pm the offer was not accepted and the sellers were moving forward with other offers.
key_points.evidence_quote: Thursday 6pm the offer was not accepted; the sellers moved forward with other offers.
key_points.reasoning: Exact time and the rejection/other-offers outcome are stated verbatim in meaning.

key_points.point_text: After viewing a newly listed house on Friday, the author decided to offer the full asking price with generous terms to avoid a bidding war and give no time for other showings, rejecting his realtor N's advice to write 10K below and negotiate upward.
key_points.evidence_quote: Friday 1pm he saw the house, liked it, and decided to offer the full asking price. / He wanted to avoid a bidding war, so he made the offer as sweet as possible with no time for other showings. / N advised writing 10K below and letting them negotiate up; the buyer was not convinced.
key_points.reasoning: All components intact: Friday viewing, full asking price, sweeteners, no time for other showings, and rejection of N's 10K-below advice.

key_points.point_text: On Friday 6pm the offer was sent at the asking price with as many favorable terms as possible and a deadline of midnight the same day.
key_points.evidence_quote: Friday 6pm they sent a sweetened offer at the asking price with a same-day midnight deadline.
key_points.reasoning: Time (Friday 6pm), asking price, sweetened/favorable terms, and same-day midnight deadline all captured.

key_points.point_text: At Friday 10:30pm the seller's realtor, who was busy driving up island, asked to extend the offer to the next midnight and mentioned in passing that another offer existed; the author extended only until 10:30am Saturday.
key_points.evidence_quote: Friday 10:30pm J was driving up island for a family thing and asked to extend the offer to Saturday midnight. / They mentioned in passing that there was another offer on the house. / Friday 11pm he extended the offer until 10:30am Saturday, reasoning a morning should be enough.
key_points.reasoning: Time, driving-up-island detail, requested extension to Saturday midnight, the passing competing-offer mention, and the partial extension to 10:30am are all preserved.

key_points.point_text: Saturday morning produced nothing, so the author suspected his offer was being kept open as leverage against other buyers and asked for disclosure of the other offer.
key_points.evidence_quote: Saturday morning nothing happened; he suspected they kept his offer open to compete and to advertise it. / N thought the other offer was better; the buyer asked them to disclose it.
key_points.reasoning: Nothing happening Saturday morning, the leverage suspicion, and the disclosure request are all captured.

key_points.point_text: On Saturday 5pm, after N reported another offer to be considered within an hour, the author dropped his offer by $20K from the asking price and removed most of the favorable terms, over N's strong advice against doing so.
key_points.evidence_quote: Saturday 5pm N relayed that another offer would be considered in an hour and they should submit in time. / He dropped the offer by 20K from asking and removed most sweeteners; N strongly advised against it.
key_points.reasoning: Time, the one-hour competing-offer relay, the 20K drop from asking, removal of sweeteners, and N's strong contrary advice are all intact.

key_points.point_text: On Saturday 7pm the seller's realtor's partner C asked N to 'fix' the price drop; meanwhile J's name was replaced by C on the REW site and removed from all four of her listings, which the author read as the seller being angry over losing $20K.
key_points.evidence_quote: Saturday 7pm C called N noticing the price drop and wondering if he could 'fix' that; N offered a counteroffer route. / J's name was removed from all her 4 listings on REW and replaced by C's; the buyer guessed they were angry about the 20K loss.
key_points.reasoning: Time (7pm), C's 'fix' request, the four-listings REW name replacement, and the 20K-anger interpretation are preserved.

key_points.point_text: At Saturday 9pm the author received a disclosure of multiple offers letter plus a counteroffer at $5K above the asking price, with a request for a response by 11pm.
key_points.evidence_quote: Saturday 9pm a disclosure of multiple offers arrived with a counteroffer 5K 'above' the asking price. / They wanted a response by 11pm; N said to respond in the morning.
key_points.reasoning: Time, disclosure-to-multiple-offers letter, the 5K-above-asking counteroffer, and 11pm response demand all captured.

key_points.point_text: On Sunday 8am the author instructed N to resubmit at 10K below the asking price, remove every favorable term, and give until 11am, as his best and final offer, rejecting N's push to meet or exceed the counteroffer.
key_points.evidence_quote: Sunday 8am he told N to update to 10K below asking, remove every sweetener, and give until 11am. / N got angry and favored the 5K-higher counter; the buyer settled on 10K below as best and final.
key_points.reasoning: Sunday 8am, 10K below asking, removal of all sweeteners, 11am deadline, best-and-final status, and rejection of N's push to meet the counter are all present.

key_points.point_text: On Sunday the author read the forwarded emails between N and the assistant L, which were unprofessional and appeared to scapegoat the assistant; the author noted they had thrown the assistant under the bus.
key_points.evidence_quote: Sunday 3pm N forwarded a series of back and forth with J's assistant L. / Sunday 5:30pm the buyer replied thanking N and saying they're throwing the assistant under the bus. / He thought the claim that the assistant missed the offer was a game, and pathetic.
key_points.reasoning: The forwarded N-L correspondence, the buyer's thrown-under-the-bus judgment, and the scapegoat/game reading are all captured.

key_points.point_text: On Monday morning the author set two explicit rules: N must not volunteer information about existing or competing offers unless explicitly asked, and any seller-agent claim of a competing offer must be provided in writing as a disclosure letter.
key_points.evidence_quote: Monday morning he thanked N and asked that competing offers never be volunteered and that agents provide disclosure letters in writing.
key_points.reasoning: Both explicit rules (no volunteering of competing offers, written disclosure letter) and the Monday morning timing are captured.

key_points.point_text: About two weeks later the house sold for 10K below the asking price, vindicating the author's read; he and N had bet a coffee, and the first house he offered on sold for way above asking.
key_points.evidence_quote: The house he first offered on later sold for waaaaay higher than the asking price. / One week later they bet a coffee: N thought the house sold 5K above asking, the buyer thought below. / Two weeks later the house sold for 10K below the asking price, so N owes him a coffee.
key_points.reasoning: Two-week outcome at 10K below asking, the coffee bet, and the first house selling well above asking are all present and consistent with the source.

key_points.point_text: The closing thesis: realtors have built a system that serves them while buyers and sellers are like pawns in a chess game, and society has given up fighting for change in countless processes from phone holders and laptops to stocks, taxes, cars, and houses.
key_points.evidence_quote: He feels realtors created a system that works fine for them, making buyers and sellers pawns in their chess game. / He compares giving up on phone holders, laptops, stocks, tax returns, cars, and houses to not wanting to fix processes.
key_points.reasoning: The realtor-serving system, buyers/sellers as pawns in a chess game, and the list of abandoned processes (phone holders, laptops, stocks, taxes, cars, houses) are all captured.
